g:greetings-fixed.title: Greetings are set phrases
g:greetings-fixed.pattern: 你好 / 您好 / 你们好
g:greetings-fixed.tip: 好 after a pronoun makes a fixed greeting with no verb: 你好 to one person, 您好 to someone you respect, 你们好 to a group. Nothing changes for the time of day.

g:apology-pair.title: Apologizing: 对不起 and 没关系
g:apology-pair.tip: 对不起 ("sorry") has an expected reply: 没关系 ("it's OK"). They travel together as a courtesy pair.

g:thanks-pair.title: Thanking: 谢谢 and 不客气
g:thanks-pair.tip: 谢谢 ("thanks") is answered with 不客气 ("you're welcome"). You can name the person thanked: 谢谢你, 谢谢你们.

g:bu-negation.title: Saying no with 不
g:bu-negation.tip: 不 negates what follows: 不客气 (not polite → you're welcome), 不好 (not good). It is the everyday "not".

g:what-shenme.title: The question word 什么
g:what-shenme.tip: 什么 means "what" and stands exactly where the answer goes, so the word order stays the same: 你叫什么名字？→ 我叫李月。

g:shi-sentence.title: The 是 sentence: A is B
g:shi-sentence.tip: 是 links two nouns, like "is/are": 我是学生 (I am a student). Negate it with 不是: 我不是老师.

g:ma-question.title: Yes-no questions with 吗
g:ma-question.tip: Add 吗 to the end of a statement to make a yes-no question, with no change in word order: 你是老师吗？ (are you a teacher?).

g:who-which.title: Asking "who" and "which" with 谁 and 哪
g:who-which.pattern: Subject + 是 + 谁 · 哪 + 国
g:who-which.tip: 谁 asks which person ("who"); 哪 asks which one out of a set. Both sit exactly where the answer will go, so the word order does not change between question and answer: 她是谁？→ 她是我的老师。

g:de-possessive.title: The possessive particle 的
g:de-possessive.tip: 的 links an owner to what they own, like English 's or "of": 我的老师 (my teacher), 他的朋友 (his friend). The owner comes first, then 的, then the thing.

g:ne-followup.title: The follow-up particle 呢 (1)
g:ne-followup.tip: 呢 turns a noun into a short "and how about …?" question that reuses the question already on the table. 我很好，你呢？ means "I'm fine, and you?" — no need to repeat the whole sentence.

g:ji-howmany.title: Asking a small number with 几
g:ji-howmany.tip: 几 asks "how many" when the answer is expected to be small (roughly under ten), and it always needs a measure word after it: 几岁 (how old), 几口人 (how many people in the family).

g:numbers-100.title: Numbers up to 100
g:numbers-100.tip: Chinese numbers stack simply: 二十 (20) is "two-ten", 二十一 (21) is "two-ten-one". Once you know 一 to 十, you can say every number up to 九十九.

g:le-change.title: 了 marking a change
g:le-change.tip: Sentence-final 了 says a new state has arrived. 她今年二十岁了 means she has now turned twenty — the 了 marks the change into that age.

g:duo-da.title: Asking age with 多大
g:duo-da.tip: 多 + an adjective asks "how ___?". 多大 literally "how big" is the ordinary way to ask an adult's age: 你多大？ For a small child you ask 几岁 instead.

g:you-family.title: Saying family size with 有
g:you-family.pattern: Subject + 家 + 有 + number + 口人
g:you-family.tip: To say how many people are in a family, use 家有 …口人: 我家有三口人 (there are three people in my family).

g:hui-learned.title: The modal verb 会 (1): a learned skill
g:hui-learned.tip: 会 before a verb means you can do something because you learned it: 我会说汉语 (I can speak Chinese), 她会做菜 (she can cook). It is about acquired skill, not permission.

g:adj-predicate.title: Adjective predicates with 很
g:adj-predicate.tip: An adjective can be the whole predicate with no 是: 菜很好吃 (the food is delicious). 很 usually fills the slot even when you do not mean "very" strongly — a bare adjective sounds like a comparison.

g:zenme-how.title: The question word 怎么 (1): how to do something
g:zenme-how.tip: 怎么 before a verb asks the manner or method: 这个字怎么读？ (how do you read this character?), 怎么写？ (how do you write it?).

g:date-1.title: Saying a date (1): month and day
g:date-1.tip: A date is built big-to-small: the month, then the day. 五月三号 is "May 3rd" (literally five-month three-day). The day of the week 星期 works the same way: 星期一 is Monday.

g:noun-predicate.title: Nominal predicates for dates and age
g:noun-predicate.tip: For dates, days and ages you can drop 是 and let the noun be the predicate: 今天三号 (today is the 3rd), 她二十岁 (she is twenty). 是 comes back when the sentence is negated with 不.

g:serial-verb-1.title: Serial verbs (1): going somewhere to do something
g:serial-verb-1.tip: Two verbs can share one subject in order of what happens: 去 + place first, then what you do there. 我去学校看书 = I go to school (and there) read.

g:xiang-want.title: The modal verb 想: wanting to do something
g:xiang-want.tip: 想 before a verb means "would like to": 我想喝茶 (I'd like to drink tea), 我想买杯子 (I want to buy a cup). On its own 想 can also mean "to miss (someone)".

g:duoshao.title: The question word 多少
g:duoshao.tip: 多少 asks "how many/how much" for any amount, large or small, and needs no measure word: 多少钱？ (how much money?). Use it, not 几, once the answer might be a big number.

g:mw-ge-kou.title: The measure words 个 and 口
g:mw-ge-kou.tip: A number cannot sit straight before a noun; a measure word goes between. 个 is the all-purpose one (三个杯子, three cups); 口 is used for counting family members (三口人).

g:money.title: Saying an amount of money
g:money.tip: 块 is the spoken word for the yuan: 三块 or 三块钱 both mean "three yuan". You may add 钱 at the end or leave it off.

g:zai-verb.title: The verb 在: being somewhere
g:zai-verb.tip: As a main verb 在 says where something is: 猫在椅子下面 (the cat is under the chair). The place comes straight after 在, with no extra "is".

g:nar-where.title: The question word 哪儿
g:nar-where.tip: 哪儿 asks "where" and stands in the place slot: 你儿子在哪儿工作？ The answer drops into the same spot: 他在医院工作。

g:zai-prep.title: The preposition 在: where an action happens
g:zai-prep.tip: Before another verb, 在 + place tells where the action happens: 他在医院工作 (he works at the hospital). The 在-phrase comes before the verb, never after it.

g:ne-location.title: The follow-up particle 呢 (2): asking where
g:ne-location.tip: 呢 after a noun can ask "where is …?" when location is what everyone is already talking about: 我的书呢？ means "Where is my book?".

g:you-exist.title: The 有 sentence: something exists somewhere
g:you-exist.tip: 有 says something is present at a place: 桌子上有电脑 (there is a computer on the table). The place comes first, then 有, then what is there.

g:he-and.title: The conjunction 和: joining nouns
g:he-and.tip: 和 links two nouns, like "and": 我和朋友 (my friend and I), 茶和水 (tea and water). It joins things, not whole sentences or verbs.

g:neng-can.title: The modal verb 能: being able / allowed
g:neng-can.tip: 能 before a verb means able or allowed to, often about the situation right now: 我能坐这儿吗？ (can I sit here?). 会 is for learned skills; 能 is for possibility and permission.

g:qing-imperative.title: Polite requests with 请
g:qing-imperative.tip: 请 before a verb makes a polite request: 请坐 (please sit), 请问 (may I ask). It softens an order into an invitation.

g:time-clock.title: Telling clock time
g:time-clock.tip: Clock time reads hour then minute: 两点十分 is 2:10 (two-o'clock ten-minutes). Note the hour "two" is 两, not 二, before 点.

g:time-adverbial.title: Time words come before the verb
g:time-adverbial.tip: A when-word sits between the subject and the verb, never after it: 我现在回家 (I'm going home now), 我们中午吃饭 (we eat at noon).

g:qian-before.title: The noun 前: "before"
g:qian-before.tip: 前 after a time span means "ago / before": 三天前 (three days ago). It follows the amount of time rather than coming in front of it.

g:zenmeyang.title: The question word 怎么样
g:zenmeyang.tip: 怎么样 asks "how is it? / how about it?": 明天天气怎么样？ (what's the weather like tomorrow?). It stands where a description would go.

g:subj-pred-predicate.title: A subject-predicate phrase as predicate
g:subj-pred-predicate.tip: A sentence can describe a topic by giving a small subject-plus-comment about part of it: 他身体很好 (as for him, his health is good). The whole "身体很好" describes 他.

g:tai-le.title: The adverb 太 … 了: too much
g:tai-le.tip: 太 before an adjective, usually closed with 了, means "too / excessively": 太热了 (it's too hot). The 了 is part of the fixed frame here.

g:hui-likely.title: The modal verb 会 (2): likely to happen
g:hui-likely.tip: 会 can also mean something is likely: 明天会下雨 (it will probably rain tomorrow). This is a prediction, different from 会 meaning a learned skill.

g:wei-interjection.title: The interjection 喂
g:wei-interjection.tip: 喂 is the standard way to open a phone call, like "hello?": 喂，你好！ It is used to get attention, not as a greeting you'd write.

g:zai-ne-progressive.title: Action in progress with 在 … 呢
g:zai-ne-progressive.tip: 在 before the verb (often closed with 呢) says the action is happening right now: 他在学做菜呢 (he is learning to cook). It marks ongoing action, like English "-ing".

g:phone-numbers.title: Reading out a phone number
g:phone-numbers.tip: Phone numbers are read one digit at a time. In this context 1 is spoken yāo instead of yī, to keep it clear over the phone.

g:ba-suggestion.title: The particle 吧: softening a suggestion
g:ba-suggestion.tip: 吧 at the end turns a statement into a gentle suggestion or guess: 我们去吧 (let's go), 你是老师吧？ (you're a teacher, right?).

g:le-completion.title: 了 marking a completed action
g:le-completion.tip: After a verb, 了 says the action happened or is finished: 她买了不少衣服 (she bought quite a few clothes). This is completion, distinct from the "change" 了 at the end of a sentence.

g:hou-after.title: The noun 后: "after"
g:hou-after.tip: 后 follows a time span or event to mean "after": 五分钟后 (after five minutes), 下课后 (after class). It comes at the end, unlike English "after".

g:a-particle.title: The particle 啊: warmth and emphasis
g:a-particle.tip: 啊 at the end adds a friendly, exclamatory tone: 真漂亮啊！ (how pretty!). It softens and warms the sentence rather than changing its meaning.

g:dou-all.title: The adverb 都: "all / both"
g:dou-all.tip: 都 sits before the verb and sums up everything mentioned before it: 这些衣服都很漂亮 (these clothes are all pretty). It looks back at the plural subject.

g:shi-de.title: The 是 … 的 structure: highlighting how/when/where
g:shi-de.tip: 是 … 的 frames the part of a past event you want to stress — when, where or how it happened: 我是坐飞机来的 (it was by plane that I came). The verb sits inside the frame.

g:date-2.title: Saying a full date (2): year, month, day
g:date-2.pattern: number + 年 + number + 月 + number + 号
g:date-2.tip: A full date runs biggest to smallest: year, then month, then day. 二〇一三年五月三号 is "May 3rd, 2013". The year is read digit by digit.

g:aux-yao.title: The auxiliary verb 要
g:aux-yao.tip: 要 before a verb expresses wanting or intending to do something — "want to" or "be going to": 我要去北京。 = I'm going to go to Beijing.

g:adv-zui.title: The adverb of degree 最
g:adv-zui.tip: 最 marks the top of a scale — "most" or "-est": 最好 = best, 最大 = biggest.

g:approx-num.title: Expressions of approximate numbers: 几 and 多
g:approx-num.tip: 几 stands for an unspecified small number ("a few / several"); a round number followed by 多 means "and then some" — 十多个 = ten-odd.

g:shi-bu-shi.title: Questions using 是不是
g:shi-bu-shi.tip: 是不是 makes a yes-no question that expects confirmation — put it before the part you are checking: 你是不是生病了？ = You're sick, aren't you?

g:pron-mei.title: The pronoun 每
g:pron-mei.tip: 每 means "every / each" and needs a measure word: 每天 = every day, 每个人 = everyone. It often pairs with 都.

g:interr-duo.title: The interrogative pronoun 多
g:interr-duo.tip: 多 before an adjective asks about degree: 多大？ = how old/big?, 多高？ = how tall?

g:de-phrase.title: The 的 phrase
g:de-phrase.tip: X + 的 with the noun left off means "the X one": 红色的 = the red one, 我的 = mine.

g:yixia.title: The numeral-measure 一下
g:yixia.tip: Verb + 一下 softens a verb to "do a bit / have a quick …": 看一下 = take a look.

g:modal-zhen.title: The modal adverb 真
g:modal-zhen.tip: 真 before an adjective voices the speaker's reaction — "really / so": 真好！ = so good! It states a feeling, unlike the neutral 很.

g:shi-de-agent.title: The 是……的 construction: emphasizing the agent
g:shi-de-agent.tip: For an action already completed, 是……的 highlights who, how or when it happened: 是他帮我介绍的 = it was he who introduced me.

g:de-shihou.title: Indicating time with ……的时候
g:de-shihou.tip: X 的时候 means "when X / at the time of X": 我小的时候 = when I was young.

g:adv-yijing.title: The adverb of time 已经
g:adv-yijing.tip: 已经 means "already" and usually pairs with 了 at the end: 他已经走了。

g:adv-jiu.title: The adverb 就
g:adv-jiu.tip: 就 here signals a quick, decisive choice — "then just …": 就买这件吧 = then just buy this one.

g:modal-hai-1.title: The modal adverb 还 (1)
g:modal-hai-1.tip: 还 adds "also / in addition": 我还要一个 = I want one more as well.

g:youdianr.title: The adverbial modifier 有点儿
g:youdianr.tip: 有点儿 + adjective means "a little (too) …", usually about something you're not happy with: 有点儿贵 = a bit expensive.

g:interr-zenme.title: The interrogative pronoun 怎么
g:interr-zenme.tip: 怎么 asks "how" or "how come": 怎么走？ = how do I get there?, 你怎么不吃了？ = how come you've stopped eating?

g:m-redup.title: Reduplication of measure words
g:m-redup.tip: Doubling a measure word means "every single one": 个个都好 = each one is good; 天天 = every day.

g:yinwei-suoyi.title: The conjunctions 因为……，所以……
g:yinwei-suoyi.tip: 因为 gives the reason and 所以 the result; Chinese keeps both halves: 因为下雨，所以我不去。

g:modal-hai-2.title: The modal adverb 还 (2)
g:modal-hai-2.tip: 还 also means "still" — an action or state that keeps going: 他还在工作。 = He is still working.

g:adv-jiu-time.title: The adverb of time 就
g:adv-jiu-time.tip: 就 stresses that something happens soon, or sooner than expected: 他六点就到了。 = He arrived as early as six.

g:verb-li.title: The verb 离
g:verb-li.tip: 离 states the distance between two places: A 离 B 远 = A is far from B. 我家离公司很近。

g:particle-ne.title: The modal particle 呢
g:particle-ne.tip: 呢 softens a question about a topic already in play, or asks "what about …?": 你呢？ = and you?; 他在做什么呢？

g:hao-ma.title: The question ……，好吗
g:hao-ma.tip: Add 好吗？ to a suggestion to ask for agreement — "…, OK?": 我们一起去，好吗？

g:adv-zai.title: The adverb 再
g:adv-zai.tip: 再 means "again / more" for something not yet done, or "(do sth) later": 明天再说 = talk about it again tomorrow.

g:pivotal.title: Pivotal sentences
g:pivotal.tip: One noun is the object of the first verb and the subject of the second: 让我想想 = let me think; 老师让我们看书。

g:verb-redup.title: Reduplication of verbs
g:verb-redup.tip: Doubling a verb makes the action brief and casual — "have a little …": 想想 = think it over a bit; 看看 = take a look.

g:result-comp.title: Complements of result
g:result-comp.tip: A result complement after a verb says how it turned out: 做完 = finish doing, 听懂 = understand (by listening), 做错 = do wrong.

g:prep-cong.title: The preposition 从
g:prep-cong.tip: 从 marks a starting point in space or time: 从这儿走 = go from here; 从九点开始。

g:di-order.title: 第- indicating order
g:di-order.tip: 第 before a number makes an ordinal: 第一 = first, 第三 = third.

g:imperative-le.title: The imperative 不要……了 / 别……了
g:imperative-le.tip: 别 or 不要 + verb + 了 tells someone to stop what they're doing: 别找了 = stop looking; 不要说了。

g:prep-dui.title: The preposition 对
g:prep-dui.tip: 对 points an action or attitude at someone: 对我说 = say to me; 他对我很好。

g:verb-attrib.title: A verb (phrase) used as an attributive modifier
g:verb-attrib.tip: A verb phrase + 的 describes a noun, like a relative clause: 说话的人 = the person who's speaking; 唱歌的孩子。

g:bi-1.title: The 比 sentence (1)
g:bi-1.tip: A 比 B + adjective compares them — "A is more … than B": 他比我大。 Don't add 很 or 太 to the adjective.

g:aux-keneng.title: The auxiliary verb 可能
g:aux-keneng.tip: 可能 before a verb marks a guess — "may / might / probably": 他可能不来了。

g:degree-comp.title: Complements of degree
g:degree-comp.tip: 得 links a verb or adjective to a comment on its degree: 穿得太少 = wear too little; 说得很好 = speak very well.

g:bi-2.title: The 比 sentence (2)
g:bi-2.tip: Put the amount of difference after the adjective: 他比我大三岁 = three years older; 便宜一点儿 = a bit cheaper.

g:particle-zhe.title: The structural particle 着
g:particle-zhe.tip: Verb + 着 marks an ongoing state that stays put: 门开着 = the door is (standing) open; 拿着书 = holding a book.

g:rhetorical-bushi.title: The rhetorical question 不是……吗
g:rhetorical-bushi.tip: 不是……吗？ states the obvious as a question — "isn't it that …?": 你不是有手机吗？ = don't you have a phone (so use it)!

g:prep-wang.title: The preposition 往
g:prep-wang.tip: 往 gives the direction of movement: 往前走 = go forward; 往右边走 = go to the right.

g:particle-guo.title: The structural particle 过
g:particle-guo.tip: Verb + 过 says something has been experienced at least once: 我看过那个电影 = I've seen that movie before.

g:suiran-danshi.title: The conjunctions 虽然……，但是……
g:suiran-danshi.tip: 虽然 concedes a point and 但是 gives the contrasting main idea; Chinese keeps both: 虽然很贵，但是很好。

g:freq-ci.title: The complement of frequency 次
g:freq-ci.tip: 次 counts how many times an action happens, placed after the verb: 去过一次 = have been once; 看了两次。

g:yao-le.title: Indicating the state of an action: 要……了
g:yao-le.tip: 要……了 says something is about to happen: 要下雨了 = it's going to rain; 新年就要到了。

g:dou-le.title: The 都……了 construction
g:dou-le.tip: 都……了 stresses that a point has already been reached — "already": 都十点了 = it's already ten; 都走了 = everyone's already left.
